title: Clone Graph
description:
Given a reference to a node in a connected undirected graph, return a deep copy of the whole graph.

Each node holds a value and a list of its neighbours:

class Node:
    def __init__(self, val=0, neighbors=None):
        self.val = val
        self.neighbors = neighbors if neighbors is not None else []

The graph is given as an adjacency list. The node at position i has value i + 1, and its entry lists the values of its neighbours. You are handed the node whose value is 1, and your answer is serialized back into the same adjacency-list form.

Every node you return must be one you built. Returning the node you were given is rejected, because copying the graph is the whole exercise.

Constraints:

  • The graph holds between 0 and 100 nodes.
  • 1 <= Node.val <= 100 and values are unique.
  • The graph is connected, undirected, and has no repeated edges or self-loops.
  • An empty graph is given as [], and you should return None.

exampleTestCases.explanation: A four node square. Each node keeps both of its neighbours after the copy.
A single node with no neighbours still has to be rebuilt rather than returned.

testCases.explanation: A four node square. Each node keeps both of its neighbours after the copy.
A single node with no neighbours still has to be rebuilt rather than returned.
The smallest real graph: two nodes joined by one edge.
A triangle, where every node reaches every other directly.
A path of five nodes, the longest chain here.
A star: the centre must be copied once even though three neighbours point at it.
A short path where the middle node has two distinct neighbours.
A four cycle written in a different order to the first case.
A five cycle, which forces the traversal to close the loop back at the start.
